items.note: It gives a clear decision: stay on pgvector, with Qdrant as the fallback. It also states the conditions that would change this.
It works out storage for 5M × 1536 (~30.7 GB raw, 60+ GB with HNSW) and projects growth to ~9M over four quarters.
The answer is built around the existing RDS PG16 setup. It credits the operational advantage of a system already in place and flags that the pgvector version available on RDS is unknown.

Every cost cell is "Unknown". The answer says pgvector is "likely inside $500/month but unverified" and never checks any option against the budget. The gap is disclosed honestly, but the constraint is not evaluated.

Tenant filtering is covered for each option: post-filter under-return and iterative scans or partitioning for pgvector, payload index, namespaces and partition key for the others. It is also part of the proposed test plan.
It compares exactly 4 options: pgvector, Qdrant, Pinecone and Milvus/Zilliz.
It provides a comparison table plus a deep-dive table, and gives one clear recommendation.
No sources were retrieved. The answer openly says it had no web access and offers no links, so the recency preference is unmet.

The structure follows the requested approach: a 4-option scan, then a deep dive on the top 2 (pgvector and Qdrant). The depth is limited because it reasons from architecture rather than from verified sources.
